discovery-weak-signals.basis: Sensor and ML deployment has company-reported operational outcomes in ignition and outage avoidance.

expectations-execution.name: financial execution
expectations-execution.basis: Year-over-year earnings improvement and reaffirmed guidance support current plan execution.

expectations-execution.name: wildfire mitigation delivery
expectations-execution.basis: Physical undergrounding and covered-line milestones provide measurable execution evidence.

expectations-execution.name: regulatory/capital burden
expectations-execution.basis: Large infrastructure investment depends on regulatory recovery, financing and customer affordability.

thesisQuality.basis: Regulated grid demand, improving earnings and measurable mitigation execution support the thesis, offset by wildfire and financing externalities.

financialOperatingMomentum.basis: Guidance was reaffirmed and current data shows TTM revenue +5.7% and net income +30%, while leverage remains material.

marketValuationOpportunity.basis: Sep. 25 valuation near 8.89x trailing and 7.35x forward earnings offers headroom but reflects wildfire/leverage risk.

catalystScore.basis: Load growth, grid investment and measurable wildfire mitigation provide multiple catalysts with conversion/regulatory uncertainty.

governancePower.basis: Current mitigation execution is improving, but historical wildfire liabilities and regulatory dependence remain material constraints.

alignment2036.basis: Reliable electricity delivery, grid expansion, wildfire resilience and electrification capacity are foundational 2036 needs.

crossDivisionLeverage.basis: Electric/gas infrastructure plus monitoring intelligence create several channels, but geography and regulated-franchise concentration remain high.

bottleneckControl.basis: The regulated transmission/distribution network is a system-critical physical bottleneck with no practical near-term substitute locally.

scenarioRobustness.basis: Electricity demand is durable, but California geography, wildfire severity, regulation and financing create concentrated exposure.

substitutionResilience.basis: Regulated grid infrastructure is exceptionally difficult to replace, though distributed resources can alter load patterns.

supplyChainResilience.basis: Large grid investment requires equipment, labor and long-lead infrastructure; exceptional supplier redundancy is not established.

pricingPower.basis: Regulated recovery supports cost pass-through while affordability and approval constrain unilateral pricing.

riskEvidence.basis: Wildfire tail liability, leverage/capital needs, regulatory recovery uncertainty, dilution and uncertain pipeline conversion are material.

dataConfidenceEvidence.basis: Two primary operating sources plus independent valuation support most factors; wildfire severity and pipeline conversion remain uncertain.

scoreRecord.thesis: Irreplaceable grid infrastructure, load growth and improving mitigation support PG&E, while wildfire, regulation and leverage sharply constrain realized economics.
scoreRecord.keyRisk: A severe wildfire, adverse regulatory recovery or financing pressure can overwhelm operating improvements and low headline valuation.
scoreRecord.nextCatalyst: Next earnings and evidence of contracted/energized load conversion with continued mitigation milestones.
